description: **CAM7 – Community Atmosphere Model version 7**  CAM7 is the atmospheric general circulation model of CESM3, developed at the NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research together with the CAM community. It simulates the resolved dynamics of the atmosphere together with parameterized turbulence, convection, clouds, precipitation, radiation, gravity-wave drag and aerosols, and is the successor to CAM6 (CESM2). CAM7 is available in two vertical configurations: a **Mid-Top (MT)** configuration extending from the surface into the upper mesosphere (~80 km) and a **Low-Top (LT)** configuration extending to the upper stratosphere (~42 km); see Section 1.  **Chemistry and aerosols** CAM7 can be run in two chemistry configurations that share the same dynamics and physics:  - **T4S (default for CMIP7):** interactive troposphere–stratosphere chemistry from the MOZART chemical family. Oxidants (OH, O₃, NO₃, H₂O₂) are computed online and used by the aerosol scheme. Aerosols are represented by the five-mode Modal Aerosol Module (MAM5), which adds a stratospheric sulfate mode to MAM4. This configuration is used for the CMIP7 spin-up and production simulations. - **SO (specified oxidants):** no interactive gas-phase chemistry; oxidant fields are prescribed from [source, e.g. climatology from a T4S simulation], greenhouse-gas concentrations are specified, and a reduced set of aerosol-precursor reactions (SO₂ → sulfate, DMS, SOAG) is computed online. Aerosols are represented by the four-mode Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4). This configuration is intended for applications where the cost of full chemistry is not justified.  Both configurations include cloud-droplet activation and ice nucleation from the aerosol population, and aerosol optical properties are computed assuming internally mixed lognormal modes.
1._grids_and_dynamical_core: **Horizontal grid.** The standard 1° configuration (`ne30pg3`) uses the spectral-element (SE) dynamical core on a cubed-sphere grid of 30 × 30 elements per face, each with 4 × 4 Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre nodes (~110 km nominal resolution). Tracer transport uses the Conservative Semi-Lagrangian Multi-tracer scheme (CSLAM), and the physics parameterizations and model output are on a separate quasi-equal-area finite-volume grid of 3 × 3 cells per element (48,600 columns globally). This SE-CSLAM configuration is described in Lauritzen et al. (2017, 2018) and Herrington et al. (2018). Variable-resolution SE grids and the MPAS dynamical core are also supported. *Horizontal discretization of the `ne30pg3` grid: (a) six cubed-sphere faces, (b) 30 × 30 spectral elements per face, (c) the 4 × 4 GLL dynamics grid and the 3 × 3 physics/output grid within one element.* **Vertical grid.** A hybrid sigma–dry-pressure (dry-mass) coordinate replaces the moist hybrid-sigma coordinate of earlier CAM versions; condensate mass is included in the total pressure. Two vertical grids are offered, both registered in the EMD: - **Mid-Top (MT, default):** 93 levels, model top near 80 km (~0.4 Pa) in the upper mesosphere. The stratosphere is resolved with ~3.5 km spacing, sufficient to internally generate a QBO. EMD vertical grid [`v162`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/vertical_computational_grid/v162.json). - **Low-Top (LT):** 58 levels, model top near 42 km (~2 hPa) in the upper stratosphere, similar in extent to CAM6 but with the CAM7 boundary-layer refinement; intended for applications where a resolved stratosphere is not required. EMD vertical grid [`v163`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/vertical_computational_grid/v163.json). Both roughly double the number of levels below 800 hPa relative to CAM6 (~16 levels, layer thickness < 200 m), with the lowest model level at ~20 m. Both share the `ne30pg3` horizontal grid, registered as EMD horizontal computational grid [`h149`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/horizontal_computational_grid/h149.json) (grid cell [`g231`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/horizontal_grid_cell/g231.json)). *Layer thickness versus height for CAM6 (32 levels), CAM7-LT (58) and CAM7-MT (93): (a) full column, (b) lowest 2 km.* **Spectral-Elelement Dynamical-core updates since CESM2.2** include orography-based reference profiles for hyperviscosity, an Exner-form pressure-gradient force, a generalized thermodynamic / major-species infrastructure, couplng with CSLAM transport scheme and updated topography generation (NCAR Topo) with Laplacian smoothing (https://github.com/NCAR/Topo). **Model For Prediction Across Scales (MPAS; https://github.com/MPAS-Dev/MPAS-Model/)** dynamical core is also supported in CESM3 and is, in particular, used for kilometer-scale (~3.75km) simulations.
2._physics_parameterizations: | Process | CAM7 scheme | |---|---| | Boundary layer, shallow convection, cloud macrophysics | CLUBB higher-order closure with prognostic momentum fluxes; active through the full MT column; CLUBB-top limiter removed | | Deep convection | The Zhang-McFarlane (1995, 2008) deep convection scheme used in CAM7 largely retains the configuration used in CAM6, using a bulk plume, mass flux approximation that consumes CAPE over a specified time scale. CAM7 includes an initial parcel calculation that is now a function of the boundary layer depth and a parallel conservative boundary layer moist static energy mixing. This reduces the sensitivity to vertical grid spacing seen with the previous configuration | | Stratiform microphysics | PUMAS (two-moment successor to MG2) with updated ice-number limiter and ice nucleation | | Radiation | RTE+RRTMGP is a modern k-distribution radiative transfer scheme that CAM7 uses as its default longwave and shortwave radiation parameterization. In CAM's implementation it's driven through and interface which maps a fixed set of 8 gases (H2O, O3, O2, CO2, N2O, CH4, CFC11, CFC12) onto either prognostic model fields or prescribed datasets, and it couples to cloud and aerosol optics | | Gravity waves / drag | Beljaars orographic form drag, anisotropic orographic GW, convective (Beres) and frontal non-orographic GW, new low-phase-speed frontal ("moving mountains") source. Moving mountain source launches a single GW phase speed per gridbox-timestep, determined by tropospheric winds. This contrasts with the broad GW spectrum launched by current frontal scheme. Amplitude of moving mountain GW is flow-dependent instead of a global constant as in current frontal scheme | | Aerosols | MAM5 with stratospheric chemistry (T4S configuration) and MAM4 for specified oxidants (SO) configuration with cloud-droplet activation and ice nucleation | | Chemistry | Extensive MOZART chemistry (T4S) or specified oxidants (SO) | *Evolution of CAM physics, dynamical cores and vertical grids from CAM4 to CAM7.*
3._notable_features_of_this_version: Relative to CAM6: raised model top and resolved stratosphere (enabling an internally generated QBO), doubled boundary-layer resolution, dry-mass vertical coordinate with condensate loading, separate physics grid with CSLAM transport, prognostic momentum fluxes in CLUBB, RTE-RRTMGP radiation, PUMAS microphysics, and a new frontal gravity-wave source. Removal of the CLUBB-top limiter and the extended RRTMGP temperature range allow stable simulation of very warm (hothouse) climates. CAM7 was tuned primarily in the coupled CESM3 system using both expert-guided and automated (QuadTune, perturbed-parameter ensemble) approaches.  A CAM7 overview paper is in preparation for JAMES (Lauritzen et al.); the reference DOI will be updated on publication.
